hookups.source: parkreservations.maryland.gov site details for sites 012, 013, 020 and 022 ('Electrical Service (amp): 30'), read 2026-10-20; DNR: 'six sites with electrical hookup'

values.note: A bathhouse at the center of the campground with hot showers and flush toilets; check-in and permits at the bathhouse, which also sells firewood ($5). A dump station with potable water.

facilities.source: https://dnr.maryland.gov/publiclands/Pages/western/gambrill.aspx ('A dump station is available for sewage and potable water. A bathhouse is located at the center of the campground, with hot showers and flush-toilets.'), read 2026-10-20

values.note: DNR: 'Reservations are now required through the entire season.' The booking page: campsites 'can be made for today and can be made up to 365 Day(s) in advance.'

The booking site lists 23 campsites: 4 electric (vehicle length 30 ft) and 19 non-electric, of which 12 take vehicles up to 20 ft and 7 are tent-only; one 20-ft site is pull-through. Plus 4 mini cabins. DNR's page says 13 basic, nine tent-only and six electric sites. Only the electric sites fit a 23-ft rig.

sites.source: https://parkreservations.maryland.gov/camping/gambrill-state-park/r/campgroundDetails.do?contractCode=MD&parkId=380110 (site type counts) + each campsiteDetails page (Max Vehicle Length, Driveway Entry), read 2026-10-20

summary: Confirmed season (first weekend in April to last weekend in October; booking site 'Open through Sat Oct 24 2026'), reservable on ReserveAmerica with a 365-day window, fees left as human-checked 2026-10-12. Added 30-amp electric, showers/flush toilets/dump/water, reservations required all season (fcfs never, over the inherited 'always'), 23 sites. Only the 4 electric sites (30 ft) fit EKKO; the other RV sites cap at 20 ft. Not stated: water/sewer at sites, minimum stay for this park, same-day cutoff time.
flags: Size: only the 4 electric sites take a vehicle over 20 ft (30 ft listed; site length 24 ft); the 12 non-electric RV sites list 20 ft and 7 are tent-only. EKKO fits, but on 4 sites only. DNR's page says six electric sites; the booking site lists four.
